general.next_condition: Next step: if you'd like, I can work out the chances for a couple where both partners carry {condition}.
general.next_general: Next step: ask me about any condition in the library, or how screening works.

not_in_library: I don't have reviewed information about that in my library, so I won't guess. A genetic counsellor can answer it properly.

risk.need_details: I can work out the chances with GeneBridge's inheritance engine. Tell me the condition and whether each parent is a carrier, affected, or neither. For example: "both parents are carriers of beta-thalassaemia".
risk.intro: For each pregnancy, when {p1} and {p2}, the chances for {condition} are:
risk.intro_both: For each pregnancy, when {both}, the chances for {condition} are:
risk.carrier: {n}% the child is a healthy carrier
risk.unaffected: {n}% the child has no changed copy
risk.same: These chances are the same for every pregnancy. Earlier children don't change them.
risk.sons: For a son: {a}% affected, {u}% not affected.
risk.daughters: For a daughter: {a}% affected, {c}% a carrier, {u}% no changed copy.
risk.xl_dom_note: Because this condition is {pattern}, the chances in a real family depend on details a genetic counsellor checks. I've added a way to talk to one.
risk.complex: {condition} is more complicated than most inherited conditions, because people have four copies of the alpha-globin genes. The chances depend on exactly which copies each parent has, so a genetic counsellor works them out from your full reports. I won't give a number that could be wrong.

parent.unaffected: one parent has no changed copy

both.unaffected: neither parent has a changed copy

xl_mother.unaffected: the mother has no changed copy

result.off: I can explain your own result if you turn on "Use my result in this chat" above the message box. I would then see only your condition and carrier status, never your raw data. For now, here's the general picture.
result.none: I couldn't find a connected result on your account. You can connect one with your reference number from your report.
result.flagged: Your result needs a genetic counsellor to explain it. It includes a finding that an app can't explain safely, and a counsellor can look at your full situation. I've marked this as a priority request, and the chat stays open for general questions.
result.carrier: Your result shows you are a healthy carrier of {condition}. You have one typical copy and one changed copy of the gene. Carriers are healthy, and this is not a diagnosis.
result.no_variant: Your result shows no changed copy was found for {condition} in the genes that were tested.
result.affected: Your result shows two changed copies for {condition}. Your own care team is the right place for questions about your health. Here I can explain what it means for children.
result.couple_both: You and {partner} both carry a changed copy of the gene for {condition}.
result.couple_one: {partner}'s result shows no changed copy for {condition}.
result.couple_not_shared: I can't see your partner's result. Both of you need to agree to the couple view before I can use it. Here is what it would mean if your partner is also a carrier:
result.turn_on_hint: Turn on "Use my result in this chat" to get an answer about your own result.

decision.lead: There isn't one right answer, and I won't choose for you. Here are the options couples in your situation have, in alphabetical order:
decision.option: {name}: {involves} Timeline: {timeline}. Cost: {cost}. A question to ask: {question}
decision.values: What matters most to you both? For example: having biological children, following religious guidance, avoiding medical procedures, cost, or your family's views.
decision.close: If it helps, the values exercise lets you each rate these privately. A genetic counsellor can also talk it through with you, whenever you're ready.
decision.reflect: You mentioned that {values} matter to you. That's an important thing to bring to any decision, and only you can weigh it.
decision.decided: It sounds like you've thought carefully about this. I can't confirm a decision for you, but a genetic counsellor can go through it with you before you take the next step. I've added a way to reach one.

pregnancy.lead: Thank you for telling me. Questions about a current pregnancy need a genetic counsellor, who can look at your full situation and talk about testing options in good time. I've marked this as a priority request.
pregnancy.no_numbers: I won't give chances for this pregnancy here; the counsellor will go through them with you.

family.lead: From the family map you shared, {condition} is seen on {sides}.
family.pattern_recessive: Because it is inherited in a recessive way, other relatives on that side may also be carriers, even if they are healthy.
family.pattern_other: Because it is {pattern}, relatives on that side may be affected differently. A genetic counsellor should go through your family with you; I've marked this as a priority request.
family.consider: People who may want to consider testing, if they choose: {relatives}. It's their decision, and they never need to know your result.
family.cousin: Your map shows a marriage between relatives. That raises the chance of a recessive condition mainly when both partners carry the same change, which screening can show.
family.offer: Would you like help drafting an anonymous message to relatives? It won't include your result.
family.not_shared: I can't see your family map. Use "Share my family map with this chat" above the message box if you'd like me to look at it for this conversation only.

prep.lead: Here are some questions you might bring to your counselling session:
q_general: What does my result mean for each pregnancy?
Which options are available to us here, and what do they involve?
Is there anyone in my family who may want testing?
What support is available while we decide?
prep.summary_note: I've drafted a one-page summary below. You can edit it before you share it; nothing is sent unless you choose to.
prep.after: Here's a plain explanation of that:
prep.after_unknown: I'm not sure what the counsellor meant by that, and I don't want to guess. It's completely fine to ask them to explain it again; that's what they're there for.

person: Of course. A genetic counsellor can talk this through with you. Use the button below to book.
distress: I'm really sorry you're going through this. What you're feeling matters, and you don't have to deal with it alone. I'll pause the genetics questions for now. If you'd like, I can connect you with a counsellor, and the people below can talk with you today.
emergency: This sounds like a medical emergency. Please call {number} now, or go to the nearest emergency department. I'll stop here so you can get help.
injection: I can't change how I work, share my instructions, or act as a doctor. I'm here to explain genetics and inheritance, and to connect you with a counsellor for anything about your own situation. What would you like to know?
off_topic: I can only help with genetics, inheritance, screening and counselling. Is there something about those I can explain?

report.lead: Here's your report, line by line:
report.line_unknown: Nothing to explain on this line.
report.redacted: Personal details were removed before I read it.
report.stop_uncertain: Part of this report needs a genetic counsellor to explain. It includes a finding that is uncertain or serious, and I won't interpret it. I've marked this as a priority request.
report.stop_differs: This report seems different from the result saved in GeneBridge. A genetic counsellor should check both before anything is explained. I've marked this as a priority request.
report.needs_ai: Reading a PDF or photo needs the full AI assistant, which isn't switched on here. You can paste the text of your report instead.

fallback: I'm sorry, I can't answer that one safely. A genetic counsellor can help, and I've added a way to reach one.
uncertain: The evidence here is limited, so I'd rather be honest than sound sure. This is a good question for a counsellor.

same_each_pregnancy.q: Quick check: is the chance the same in every pregnancy?
same_each_pregnancy.right: That's right. Each pregnancy has the same chances, whatever happened before.
same_each_pregnancy.wrong: Not quite. The chances are the same every time; earlier children don't change them for the next pregnancy.

carrier_healthy.q: Quick check: is a carrier usually healthy?
carrier_healthy.right: That's right. Carriers are healthy; being a carrier matters mainly when planning a family.
carrier_healthy.wrong: Not quite. Carriers are healthy. Being a carrier matters mainly when planning a family.

self_status.lead: GeneBridge can't tell whether you have or carry {condition} from what you describe. Only a genetic test can tell you.
self_status.lead_general: GeneBridge can't tell whether you have or carry a condition from what you describe. Only a genetic test can tell you.
self_status.family: If a close relative, such as a brother or sister, has it, there is a real chance you carry it too, but only a test can tell you.
self_status.next: Free, confidential testing is available, and a genetic counsellor can help you decide whether and when to be tested.
